analysis.title: GS US TMT .. quick hits + earnings (NXP, Visa, STX, APH & more)..
key_insights: Market breadth is narrow, with about 60% of S&P names lower on the day, while the NDX is up +135 bps and trying to post back-to-back >1% daily gains for the first time in about 3 months, in an 'AI vs the rest' trade.

The TMT trader (P. Bartlett) says the bounce still looks driven by supply abatement as high-velocity supply and length reduction recede. The tape is testing whether the 'bounce' turns into a 'rally' as headwinds ease (positioning/valuations, earnings t+1 reactions, financing, rates angst) ahead of FOMC tomorrow, Mag 7 earnings over the next few days and the US midterm election next week.

Some Software/Services names (payroll names, fin/biz services, pockets of SaaS) are quietly back near 52-week highs. A number of AI/supply chain names are down about 30-50% from YTD highs and trade below trend lines and 200-dma. The desk asks whether this is a 'tell' or an 'opportunity' into 2027.
YTD normalized chart: the SPX ex-AI index (SPXXAI) is reeling after a test of its all-time highs, while the NDX is bouncing off the lows of its summer trading range.

Top client inbounds today: SPOT giving back gains, software weakness (TWLO, IOT, INTU), whether to chase the semis/AI move or whether it is all covering, AMZN's intraday rally, CDNS breakout potential, FWONK's trough multiple, and DASH's rally.
Earnings tonight with the most questions: CSGP, FFIV, SK Hynix, LOGI, NXPI, ST, STX, TER, Visa. Tomorrow morning: APH, Dassault Systemes, EDU, FLEX, GEV, VRT.

NXPI debate centers on mix (AI/datacenter vs autos) and gross margins. The stock arguably trades closer to auto/connector peers (ST, TEL) than to broad analog peers (ADI, TXN). Consensus revenue is +7% q/q for September and +3% q/q for December, after a strong TXN print last week (auto segment revenue +10% q/q). NXPI has been lower on 8 of 9 prints on a t+1 basis.

Memory debate into prints this week: how to reconcile still-strong memory prices and supply/demand plus transitions that cap returns against compressing multiples. GIR published takes from a TrendForce webinar that are positive on DRAM pricing through 2027 and into 1H28.

STX is about 50% off its highs but still up +100% on the year. After WDC's strong results last week (mid/high-teens q/q revenue growth vs Seagate consensus closer to low double digits q/q), focus is on STX execution (especially HAMR), incremental margins and industry supply/demand commentary into 2027+ (capex, crossbars). Seagate has beaten EPS by double-digit percentages over recent prints and finished higher on 9 of 11 prints at t+1.

Visa debate per GIR's EPS preview centers on how much VAS revenue decelerates toward more normalized growth after a year of standout organic growth and one-off contributors (World Cup and Olympics marketing, US fiscal stimulus). Historically tough September seasonality has given way to more constructive 4Q action.

APH's multiple has compressed toward about 5-year lows despite a solid 2Q report about 90 days ago (orders +63% organically y/y, book-to-bill above 1 in all end markets). The debate focuses on copper/optics and the duration of the AI cycle.

sector_views.rationale: The desk frames an 'AI vs the rest' tape with AI/supply chain names down 30-50% from YTD highs and software/services near 52-week highs, and asks whether that is a tell or an opportunity without taking a side.

earnings_insights: NXPI reports tonight: consensus revenue +7% q/q for September and +3% q/q for December (estimates, not reported). TXN's print last week showed auto segment revenue +10% q/q (reported). NXPI has fallen on 8 of 9 prints on t+1.

STX reports tonight: Seagate consensus revenue growth is closer to low double digits q/q (estimate), versus WDC's mid/high-teens q/q revenue growth (reported last week). Seagate has beaten EPS by double-digit percentages over recent prints and rose on 9 of 11 prints at t+1.
Visa reports tonight: GIR's EPS preview focuses on how far VAS revenue growth decelerates after standout organic growth aided by one-offs (World Cup and Olympics marketing, US fiscal stimulus).
APH reports tomorrow morning: the 2Q report about 90 days ago showed orders +63% organically y/y with book-to-bill above 1 in all end markets (reported). The multiple is near 5-year lows.
Also reporting tonight: CSGP, FFIV, SK Hynix, LOGI, ST, TER. Tomorrow morning: Dassault Systemes, EDU, FLEX, GEV, VRT.
risk_factors: FOMC tomorrow, Mag 7 earnings over the next few days and the US midterm election next week are near-term event risks.

AI cycle duration and copper/optics demand are the debate for APH.
VAS revenue deceleration and fading one-off contributors are the debate for Visa.
NXPI mix and gross margin uncertainty, with a history of falling after earnings.

tension_points.bull_case: Supply-driven selling is abating and headwinds (positioning, valuations, earnings reactions, financing, rates) may ease, so the NDX bounce could turn into a rally. AI/supply chain names down 30-50% from highs could be an opportunity into 2027.
tension_points.bear_case: Breadth is narrow, with about 60% of S&P names lower, and many AI/supply chain charts sit below trend lines and 200-dma. Software/services strength near 52-week highs could be a tell that the AI trade is weakening.
tension_points.what_invalidates: FOMC tomorrow, Mag 7 earnings over the next few days and the US midterm election next week are the named events that decide whether the bounce becomes a rally.

tension_points.bull_case: GIR is positive on DRAM pricing through 2027 and into 1H28, and memory prices and supply/demand remain strong.
tension_points.bear_case: Transitions that cap returns and compressing multiples complicate the case.
tension_points.what_invalidates: This week's memory prints, including SK Hynix tonight, are the named test.
